title: Extraordinary mechanical properties of AZ61 alloy processed by ECAP with 160 deg channel angle and EPT

nodes.label: Rare-earth-free AZ61 needs both high strength and good ductility; conventional/SPD routes give unbalanced properties

attrs.basis: discussion text on F13/F14; packet has no introduction

nodes.label: Low-strain 160-degree ECAP stores high dislocation energy; EPT then statically recrystallizes it into ultrafine homogeneous grains
Commercial hot-extruded AZ61 plate, homogenized 623 K 4 h, as starting material
Combine ECAP with 160-degree channel die (Bc route) and subsequent electropulsing treatment
160-degree die imposes low equivalent strain per pass (~0.2) versus 90-degree dies
ECAP temperature (373/423/473 K) x passes (2-5, 8); EPT pulse duration (25-50 us) x time (5-20 min)
ECAP of AZ61 billets at 373, 423, 473 K for 2-5 passes
373 K: deformed portion rises markedly from 2 to 3-4 passes; undeformed area dominant at 2 passes

attrs.image_note: (a) twin-laden coarse grains; (b,c) dense crossing deformation bands cover nearly the whole field

nodes.label: Samples fracture at 5th ECAP pass at 373 K; at 423 K 5 passes succeed
DRX appears locally at 4 passes and in most areas at 5 passes (423 K); earlier and coarser at 473 K

attrs.image_note: At 50 um scale F4 shows twins and deformation bands; DRX grains in (c,d) are not individually resolved, (d) only shows a finer dark-etched texture

nodes.label: Select 373K-4 samples (highest defect density) and design variable-temperature ECAP (423K-8 + 373K-3) for EPT

attrs.reason: 373 K cannot exceed 4 passes; higher T triggers DRX that consumes stored energy

nodes.label: Variable-temperature ECAP: 8 passes at 423 K then 3 passes at 373 K
423K-8: grains markedly refined but not equiaxed; after +373K-3 refined and further elongated

attrs.image_note: Both panels show a dense fine etched structure at 10 um scale; refinement (b vs a) visible, but grain elongation/equiaxedness not resolvable

nodes.label: Low-temperature (373 K / variable-T) ECAP suppresses DRX and accumulates high dislocation density (stored energy)

attrs.basis: inferred from incomplete DRX; dislocation density not measured

nodes.label: Electropulsing treatment of ECAPed samples: 25-50 us pulses, 5-20 min, 100 Hz
EPT on 373K-4: recrystallization grows with time, full at 30us-10min; abnormal growth at longer time/pulse; 473K-ECAP gives coarse uneven grains

attrs.image_note: F7 a->c partial to full equiaxed SRX, e/f coarse grains shown; F8 a deformed/twinned, d finest uniform grains; caption vs text disagree on pass numbers for F8 (4 vs 3) and F9 (3 vs 4)

nodes.label: Variable-T ECAP + EPT: 25us-10min gives uniform ~1 um equiaxed grains; 30us-7/10min ~2.5/3 um (abnormal growth)

attrs.image_note: (d) is a rough etched fine structure where boundaries are hard to delineate; (b,c) show 1-3 um grains that look fairly unimodal rather than abnormal

nodes.label: EBSD orientation maps: ultrafine equiaxed grains (~1 um) at 25us-10min, visibly coarser at 30us-10min

attrs.image_note: IPF maps clearly show ~1 um equiaxed grains (a) vs ~2-3 um (c)

nodes.label: Grain size refined from 89 um to ~1.0 um, homogeneous and equiaxed, after variable-T ECAP + 25us-10min EPT
High ECAP stored energy plus instantaneous high-energy pulse completes static recrystallization in short time; low stored energy (high-T ECAP) leads to growth
Fine bright second-phase particles dispersed throughout EPT samples

attrs.image_note: Bright sub-100 nm particles visible in all four panels, densest in (b,c); phase identity (Mg17Al12) is not shown by any figure

nodes.label: Second phase (stated Mg17Al12) precipitated and dispersed by EPT
(0001) pole figures: max 3.85 MRD at 25us-10min with maxima toward TD rim; 4.57 at 30us-10min

attrs.image_note: Maxima sit near the TD rim, not at the centre (ND); no pre-EPT pole figure is shown, so 'weakened' has no baseline in the figure

nodes.label: Misorientation histograms: LAGB 20%, HAGB 65% (25 us); HAGB rises to 90% with broad 15-90 deg distribution (30 us)

attrs.image_note: (b) dominated by a <2 deg bin (0.155) that is hard to reconcile with 20% LAGB in 2-10 deg; (d) broad 15-90 deg shelf shown

nodes.label: Histograms show a distinct ~30 deg peak (25 us) and a spike at ~86-90 deg (30 us), unmentioned in text

attrs.possible_meaning: ~86 deg is the {10-12} extension-twin misorientation in Mg; ~30 deg <0001> rotation typical of recrystallized Mg

nodes.label: EPT weakens basal texture and raises HAGB fraction (65 -> 90%) through static recrystallization
ECAP raises YS/UTS but lowers TEF (373K-4: 300/360 MPa, 7%); higher T lowers YS, raises TEF; 423K-8(+373K-3) strongest

attrs.image_note: Curves agree with text ranking; as-received true-stress peak ~300 MPa vs 260 MPa quoted (Table 2 likely engineering)

nodes.label: YS rises monotonically with passes at 373 K (to 300 MPa); at 423 K peaks at 4 passes then falls at 5

attrs.image_note: Also shows 1-pass crossing (423 K > 373 K), not discussed

nodes.label: ECAP strengthens AZ61 strongly (YS 100 -> 300-350 MPa) at the cost of ductility
sigma_ys = sigma_GB (Hall-Petch) + sigma_P (precipitation) + sigma_dislocation
ECAP strength rise mainly from dislocation strengthening, plus grain-boundary and Mg17Al12 precipitation strengthening
423K-8+373K-3+25us-10min: YS 330 MPa, UTS 448 MPa, TEF 15%

attrs.image_note: Blue curve: yield knee ~330-340 MPa, peak ~448 MPa, failure strain ~0.15

nodes.label: After EPT, YS decreases while UTS and TEF increase relative to the ECAPed state

attrs.comparison: F12 vs F13 same starting states

nodes.label: ECAP+EPT AZ61 reaches YS 330, UTS 448 MPa with TEF 15%: best strength-ductility combination
EPT recovery/SRX removes stress concentration and dislocation tangles, weakening dislocation strengthening
Loss of dislocation strengthening is offset by ultrafine homogeneous grains and dispersed precipitates, restoring ductility
Weakened basal texture and high HAGB fraction activate non-basal slip/GB sliding, raising elongation
In UTS-vs-YS map this work's points lie up-right of all literature AZ61 routes

attrs.image_note: Three red points (~275/380, 295/355, 335/448 MPa) exceed all 10 other routes in both axes

nodes.label: AZ61 by conventional deformation or SPD has unbalanced UTS/YS; ECAP+EPT gives markedly higher strength and ductility
Use high-stored-energy low-T ECAP then short-pulse EPT (25 us, 10 min); longer pulses/times or high-T ECAP cause grain growth
160-degree ECAP + EPT produces homogeneous ultrafine grains and extraordinary strength-ductility in RE-free AZ61

notes: Packet has no introduction text, so HYP nodes are inferred. Lost: per-sample Table 1-3 values, the 473 K ECAP branch detail (F5), as-received/homogenized micrographs (F2). Branch points: (i) ECAP-only strengthening line (n27-n31) vs ECAP+EPT balance line (n32-n36); (ii) the ductility argument via texture/HAGB (n37) exists only in MatMech extraction; packet text for F11 truncates. Image audit: F11 pole figure has no pre-EPT baseline, maxima lie near TD so 'basal texture weakened' is not shown; F11b <2 deg bin dominates the histogram; F11d has an unmentioned ~86-90 deg spike (extension twins?) that would inflate the HAGB fraction attributed to SRX (n25 qualifies n26). F10d SEM does not resolve the ~1 um equiaxed grains that the EBSD map (F11a) does show. F8/F9 captions disagree with text on pass numbers. Precipitate identity Mg17Al12 never shown. n14 dislocation density is never measured (fit poor: STR/defect/extended used for 'stored energy'). n41 -> n2 supports records the conclusion confirming the inferred hypothesis.
